grammar_rules.rule_name: Demonstrative adjectives agree in gender and number
grammar_rules.summary: Demonstrative adjectives (ce, cet, cette, ces) agree with the noun they modify.
grammar_rules.explanation: Demonstrative adjectives point out specific nouns and agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.
grammar_rules.formation: Masculine singular: ce before consonant, cet before vowel or mute h; feminine singular: cette; plural (masculine and feminine): ces.
usage: Pointing out specific people or things
restrictions: ce becomes cet only before a masculine singular noun beginning with a vowel or mute h.
ce itself is not used before such nouns.
conditions: A demonstrative adjective points out a specific noun.
The form ce/cet/cette/ces agrees in gender and number with that noun; cet precedes a masculine singular noun beginning with a vowel or mute h.
exceptions: ce becomes cet before masculine singular noun starting with a vowel or mute h (e.g., cet appartement, cet arbre).
agreement_rules: Agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.
transformations: ce -> cet before vowel or mute h: ce livre -> cet auteur, cet homme
ce -> cette (feminine): ce livre -> cette revue
ce -> ces (plural): ce livre -> ces livres
common_traps: Confusing ce and cet; forgetting that cet is used before vowel or mute h.

sources.source_text: Masculine singular ce livre, cet auteur, cet homme; note that ce adds -t before masculine singular noun starting with vowel or mute h.
